payload.title: Remote-only mode is unusable: uncached N+1 reads exceed max_execution_time and truncate pages
payload.body:
## Summary
Remote-only operation is not viable today: a single page issues dozens of sequential HTTP round trips to `/remotedb` and exceeds `max_execution_time`.

## Reproduction
Point an instance at the remote endpoint with no local MySQL and open `/consult`:
```
Fatal error: Maximum execution time of 30 seconds exceeded in
app/Services/DatabaseService.php on line 25
```
Line 25 is `curl_exec()` in `remoteCall()`. The HTML truncates mid-render — on `/consult` this cut off the search `<script>`, so the search box rendered with no behaviour at all.

## Pinpointed cause
`DatabaseService` has no request-level caching. `read()` performs a full-table fetch every time it is called, and a page calls it repeatedly (settings, secrets, astrologers, reviews per astrologer, categories...). On local MySQL this is merely wasteful; over HTTP it is fatal.

Two aggravating factors:
- `remoteCall()` returns `[]` on any non-200, so failures are silent rather than loud.
- `find()` with a non-`id` key falls back to `read()` — a full table fetch per lookup.

## Intended scope
This blocks the goal of running purely against the remote MySQL API. Add a request-level memo to `read()` with invalidation on write, collapse the per-astrologer review lookups, and make transport failures raise instead of returning `[]`.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] `/consult`, `/shop` and `/` render fully in remote-only mode inside the default execution limit
- [ ] Remote transport errors surface instead of silently emptying the page
- [ ] Repeated `read()` of the same collection in one request hits the remote endpoint once
